title: GeoCore-9B: Towards Geo-Aware Generative Foundation Models in Earth Observation
claim: A generative model trained with flow matching plus a training-only distillation loss from a frozen teacher gains structural fidelity at no inference cost.
layout: Single wide panel, left-to-right flow, inference box inset top-right, frozen/trainable icons
description: A wide block diagram labeled Training on the left, with a pink-bordered Inference inset at the top right. An EO satellite image x passes through a frozen VAE encoder to give latent z1. A linear trajectory blends z1 with Gaussian noise z0 to produce the noisy latent zt, which enters a row of gray DiT Blocks. Text and metadata conditions come in from the bottom. The text goes through frozen local and global text encoders, and a globe icon marks the GSD, latitude and longitude metadata. These combine with the timestep into a condition c that drives AdaLN modulation. At the top, an orange teacher feature extractor produces geospatial priors. A red arrow marks the Geospatial Semantic Alignment loss on a trainable projection head. A blue arrow marks the flow-matching loss against the target velocity. Snowflake and flame icons mark frozen and trainable modules. Color-coded boxes and equations label each stage. The inference inset shows an ODE solver feeding the VAE decoder, which outputs x̂.
caption: Overview of GeoCore-9B. GeoCore-9B trains a Flow Matching-based DiT in the latent space, conditioned on local text tokens and global geospatial metadata through token fusion and AdaLN. A training-only Geospatial Semantic Alignment loss distills structural Earth priors from a frozen satellite-specialist teacher, improving spatial fidelity without adding inference overhead.
abstract: Existing generative models for earth observation (EO) predominantly rely on fine-tuning natural image priors, which limits their scalability and introduces perspective biases that conflict with geospatial constraints. To address this, we introduce GeoCore-9B, a 9-billion-parameter generative foundation model, which is the first of its scale to be trained from scratch exclusively on EO data. Unlike previous EO foundation models, GeoCore-9B is built upon a Flow Matching-based Diffusion Transformer (DiT) and natively conditions generation on text descriptions and continuous geospatial metadata, including ground sample distances, latitudes, and longitudes. To overcome the convergence and spatial disorientation challenges of training at this scale, we propose a Geospatial Semantic Alignment loss. This objective distills structural Earth surface priors (e.g., terrain and urban areas) from a frozen specialist teacher network, constraining the diffusion latent trajectory during training without adding inference overhead. Pre-trained on the global-scale Git-10M dataset, GeoCore-9B demonstrates strong downstream versatility. Beyond standard proxy generative tasks, we show that GeoCore-9B can be effectively adapted for practical EO applications, including highly challenging tasks such as cloud removal and SAR-to-optical cross-modal translation. Extensive evaluations confirm that GeoCore-9B establishes new state-of-the-art performance in both visual fidelity and geographic structural accuracy.
